name: ESP32-C2

strapping.8: Chip boot mode (with GPIO9) and UART0 ROM message printing (with EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL). No default pull at reset (datasheet: 'N/A'). For Joint Download Boot GPIO8 must be 1 while GPIO9=0; GPIO8 is don't-care for SPI boot. Must therefore be externally defined if download mode is needed.
strapping.9: Chip boot mode. Default internal weak pull-up (1). GPIO9=1 -> SPI boot; GPIO9=0 (with GPIO8=1) -> Joint Download Boot (UART download).

psram.condition: Not applicable: no PSRAM in the ESP8684 series comparison table and the ESP-IDF GPIO page mentions only SPI flash for SPI0/1.

usb_jtag.note: ESP32-C2 / ESP8684 has no USB peripheral (no USB-Serial-JTAG, no USB OTG) in the ESP8684 datasheet. Console/flashing via UART0.

notes: JTAG mapping (ESP8684 datasheet IO MUX Table 4): MTMS=GPIO4, MTDI=GPIO5, MTCK=GPIO6, MTDO=GPIO7. These overlap ADC1_CH4 (GPIO4) and the RTC/deep-sleep-wakeup-capable GPIO0-5.

ESP-IDF GPIO page: 'The ESP32-C2 chip features 21 physical GPIO pins (GPIO0 ~ GPIO20). For chip variants with an SiP flash built in, GPIO11 ~ GPIO17 are dedicated to connecting the SiP flash; therefore, only 14 GPIO pins are available.' The ESP8684 (all current parts have in-package flash: ESP8684H2X/H4X) bonds out only GPIO0-10 and GPIO18-20.

flash_spi discrepancy inside the ESP-IDF GPIO page: the table/note mark only GPIO12-17 as 'SPI0/1 ... usually used for SPI flash', while the summary sentence says GPIO11-17 are dedicated to SiP flash. flash_spi uses the conservative 11-17; GPIO11's exact role is not stated in the sources consulted.

Only one SAR ADC (ADC1, 5 channels on GPIO0-4) per ESP-IDF GPIO page and ESP8684 datasheet ('12-bit SAR ADC, up to 5 channels', 'One DIG ADC controller'). No ADC2 pins -> adc2 empty and adc2_wifi_conflict null. The ESP-IDF C2 ADC oneshot 'Hardware Limitations' has no ADC2/Wi-Fi item.
No ADC continuous-mode page exists for esp32c2 in ESP-IDF stable docs (fetch returned no Hardware Limitations section).
ESP-IDF GPIO page: 'GPIO0-5 can be used to wake up the chip from Deep-sleep mode. Other GPIOs can only wake up the chip from Light-sleep mode.'
No input-only pins: all IO MUX functions are I/O/T in the datasheet and the ESP-IDF page lists no GPI pins.
Strapping hold time t1 min 3 ms after CHIP_EN goes high (datasheet Table 11). GPIO8=0 with GPIO9=0 is not a listed boot mode.
Datasheet: U0TXD (GPIO20) is output-enabled with weak pull-up after reset; U0RXD (GPIO19) input with weak pull-up; GPIO9 has weak pull-up after reset.
ESP-IDF refers to the ESP8684 datasheet for this target; the strapping/pin data here come from ESP8684 Series Datasheet v2.3.
Datasheet section 3.3: ROM bootloader assumes a 40 MHz crystal; with a 26 MHz crystal the ROM UART baud is ~74880.
toolchain_prefix confirmed from ESP-IDF docs: riscv32-esp-elf-gdb and riscv32-esp-elf-addr2line.
sources: https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp8684_datasheet_en.pdf (v2.3: Table 1, Table 2 Pin Overview, Table 3/4 IO MUX, Table 6 Analog Functions, Section 2.3.3, Section 3 Boot Configurations, Section 4.2.2.1 SAR ADC)
